Project: Kubernetes. Upgrade being assessed: 1.23 -> 1.29.
This change was introduced in release 1.26. Source: Kubernetes v1.26.0 CHANGELOG (official_changelog). Section: v1.26.0 / Changes by Kind / Deprecation.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
The gcp and azure auth plugins have been removed from client-go and kubectl. See kubelogin and Kubectl Auth Changes in GKE for details about the cloud-specific replacements.
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
v1.26.0 / Changes by Kind / Deprecation: CLI flag pod-eviction-timeout is deprecated and will be removed together with enable-taint-manager in v1.27. Kube-apiserver: the unused --master-service-namespace flag was deprecated and will be removed in v1.27. The gcp and azure auth plugins have been removed from client-go and kubectl. See kubelogin and Kubectl Auth Changes in GKE for details about the cloud-specific replacements.
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 1.29 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 1.26 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: Removed gcp and azure auth plugins in client-go and kubectl
paths.description: The gcp and azure auth plugins were removed from client-go and kubectl in 1.26. Kubeconfigs or client-go based applications that rely on these plugins will no longer be able to authenticate through them and must move to the cloud-specific replacements (kubelogin for Azure, and the GKE kubectl auth changes for GCP).

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 1.26, where the gcp and azure auth plugins were removed from client-go and kubectl.
quotes: The gcp and azure auth plugins have been removed from client-go and kubectl.
conditions.relevance: Ties the removal to release 1.26 which is crossed when upgrading from 1.23 to 1.29.

conditions.statement: A kubeconfig (users/auth-provider entries) or client-go based application uses the gcp or azure auth plugin to authenticate.
quotes: The gcp and azure auth plugins have been removed from client-go and kubectl.
conditions.relevance: The text names the gcp and azure auth plugins as the removed components, so any usage of them is affected.
ambiguities: The text does not state the exact kubeconfig syntax used to reference these plugins.

conditions.statement: Client tooling is kubectl or client-go from release 1.26 or later, where the plugins are no longer included.
quotes: have been removed from client-go and kubectl
conditions.relevance: The break occurs only when the client binaries or libraries in use are at or after the version that removed the plugins.
ambiguities: The text does not state whether clients older than 1.26 continue to work against a 1.29 cluster.

suggested_actions: Replace the azure auth-provider configuration with kubelogin (exec-based credential plugin).
For GCP, follow the 'Kubectl Auth Changes in GKE' guidance to switch to the cloud-specific replacement.
Update kubeconfig files and CI/automation that use gcp or azure auth-provider entries before upgrading kubectl or client-go to 1.26 or later.
Rebuild applications that import the gcp or azure client-go auth plugins against the replacement mechanism.
